sections.heading: Know Your Numbers: Business Costs and Hourly Rates
sections.body: Before you even think about how to quote driveway pressure cleaning, you need to nail down your own business costs. This means knowing your overheads like insurance, equipment depreciation, fuel, detergents, and your own hourly wage. A common mistake is just guessing. Add up your monthly fixed costs, then divide by the average number of hours you work. For example, if your ute, pressure washer, and chemicals cost you $1500 a month and you work 160 hours, that's almost $10 an hour before you even pay yourself. Factor in your desired hourly rate, usually $50-$80 an hour for skilled work, and you've got a baseline. Your pressure wash quote needs to cover these expenses and leave a profit. Don't forget the wear and tear on your gear, which can be significant with commercial pressure washing. Track these numbers closely to ensure every concrete cleaning price you provide is profitable. A 4000 PSI commercial-grade pressure washer might cost $2000-$5000, and its lifespan depends on how well you maintain it.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Pricing Method: Per Square Metre or Flat Rate?
sections.body: The most straightforward way to price driveway cleaning is per square metre for most residential jobs. This method gives you a clear, consistent figure based on the actual size of the area. Get your measuring wheel out or use satellite tools if the property is accessible. A common rate in Australia for basic concrete driveway cleaning ranges from $2.50 to $5.00 per square metre, depending on the factors listed below. For smaller jobs or those with complex layouts, a flat rate might be easier to manage and explain to the client. This is particularly useful for things like small courtyard areas or paved walkways that aren't a simple rectangle. Always specify what's included in either method – basic clean, chemical pre-treatment, post-clean sealer, etc. This clarity prevents misunderstandings and makes your driveway cleaning cost transparent. For example, a 60 square metre standard driveway at $3.50/sqm would be $210, plus GST.

sections.heading: On-Site Job Assessment: What to Look For
sections.body: Before you finalise any pressure wash quote, a thorough on-site assessment is crucial. Look at the type of surface (concrete, pavers, asphalt), the level of grime (algae, oil stains, mould), and the access to water and drainage. Is there easy access for your equipment? Are there delicate plants nearby that need protecting? Are there any slip hazards you need to manage? Photos are your best friend here – take before shots and use them when explaining the work to the client. Also, note any repairs needed before cleaning, like loose pavers or cracks in concrete, as these can affect your process or even become liability issues. A badly degraded concrete surface might require a gentler approach or specific chemicals, impacting your concrete cleaning price. Always check local council regulations for water runoff, especially regarding chemical use; you might need to capture and dispose of wastewater responsibly. You can find guidance on managing chemical runoff from your local environmental protection authority, often via a .gov.au website.

sections.heading: Factoring in Variables: Dirt, Surface Type, and Obstacles
sections.body: Every driveway pressure cleaning job is different, and your quote needs to reflect these variables. Heavy oil stains, rust marks, or deep-seated mould will require specific pre-treatment chemicals and more time than a light dust clean. Different surfaces also demand different approaches: pavers need careful attention to sand infill, while exposed aggregate concrete has its own challenges. Obstacles like parked cars, bins, or garden furniture that need moving will add time to the job, so factor that into your hourly rate. Are there significant inclines or tricky corners? This can slow you down. Always build a small contingency into your driveway cleaning cost for unexpected issues, maybe 10-15% of the total labour. For instance, removing a 10sqm patch of heavy oil stain might add an extra $50-$100 in chemical costs and 30 minutes of labour.

sections.heading: Crafting a Professional Pressure Wash Quote with QuoteMate
sections.body: Your quote isn't just a price; it's a reflection of your professionalism. A clear, itemised quote builds trust and helps the client understand exactly what they're paying for. Detail your services: pre-treatment, pressure washing, post-clean rinse, and any optional extras like sealing. Break down your costs, showing labour, materials (e.g., specific detergents at $30-$50 per litre), and equipment use if relevant. Use clear language, avoid jargon, and ensure all prices include GST. With QuoteMate, you can quickly generate professional PDF quotes that outline all these details, send them directly to the client, and track their status. This makes managing your pressure wash quote process simple and keeps you looking sharp. Always include your terms and conditions, such as payment schedules (e.g., 50% upfront for larger jobs) and guarantees, to protect both you and the client.

sections.heading: Common Quoting Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
sections.body: The quickest way to lose money on a job is to underquote or miss crucial details. Don't guess the size of the driveway; measure it. Don't assume the dirt level; inspect it closely. Not accounting for water source limitations or drainage issues can lead to costly delays. Another common error is forgetting to add GST to your final figure. Always specify your inclusions and exclusions to avoid scope creep – where the client expects more than what was agreed. For instance, if the quote is just for the driveway, make sure they don't expect the front path to be cleaned for free. Review your quotes before sending them out, and use a checklist to ensure you've covered all bases from access to chemical disposal. For any commercial or public area work, ensure you adhere to Australian Standard AS/NZS 3000 for electrical safety when using powered equipment. A 100 square metre job, if misquoted by just $1 per square metre, means you're out $100 profit.

tips: Always measure the driveway accurately; never guess the size.
Factor in chemical costs for specific stains like oil or rust.
Charge more for heavily soiled driveways needing pre-treatment and longer cleaning times.
Clearly list what's included and excluded in your quote to prevent client disputes.
Always confirm access to a water source and adequate drainage before starting.
Build a 10-15% contingency into your quote for unexpected issues or extra time.

guides.title: Pricing Your Pest Inspections: A Guide on How to Quote Pest Inspection Jobs

guides.description: Learn how to quote pest inspection jobs accurately for Australian properties. Cover all costs, from basic checks to comprehensive termite reports, and boost your business.

sections.heading: Understanding Standard Pest Inspection Costs for Australian Properties
sections.body: To nail your profit margins as a pest controller, you need to know how to quote pest inspection jobs accurately. A standard visual pest inspection for a typical 3-bedroom home usually sits between $250 and $450, depending on your location and the property's accessibility. Don't just throw out a number; a precise quote covers your time, travel, and the detailed report expected by clients. For example, a thorough pre-purchase pest inspection, critical for homebuyers, demands more than a quick visual check. It requires detailed attention to timber pests and potential structural issues, justifying a higher fee. Your reputation rides on providing clear, comprehensive quotes that stand up to scrutiny, ensuring both you and your client know exactly what to expect from the service. Get it right, and you'll build trust and a solid client base. Most basic inspections take around 1.5 to 2 hours on site, not including travel or report writing time.

sections.heading: Key Factors Driving Your Pest Inspection Quote Prices
sections.body: Your quote needs to reflect the scope and complexity of the job. The biggest factors influencing the price include property size, accessibility, and the type of pests suspected or targeted. A large, multi-level house with restricted subfloor or roof void access will take longer and cost more to inspect than a small, single-storey unit on a slab. Travel time is another big one; factor in your fuel and time spent getting to and from the site. If the property is rural, the travel component of your pest report price will naturally be higher. Always ask about the property's construction type and any known pest issues upfront. For a standard 200m² home, expect around $1.80-$2.20 per square metre for a comprehensive inspection, or around $350-$440.

sections.heading: Pricing Different Types of Pest Inspections and Reports
sections.body: Not all pest inspections are created equal, and your pricing should reflect that. A basic visual pest inspection, often a general check for common pests like spiders and cockroaches, will be your lowest tier. Pre-purchase pest inspection services, which are critical for property transactions, must comply with Australian Standard AS 4349.3. These require thorough checks for timber pests like termites and borers, and their comprehensive nature commands a higher fee, typically ranging from $350 to $650 for an average home. A dedicated termite inspection cost is usually at the higher end, especially if it includes thermal imaging or invasive checks (with client permission). Always be clear about what each service includes. A combined building and pest inspection, often offered by property inspection firms, can push the total cost above $700, showing the value clients place on a thorough report.

sections.heading: Building a Comprehensive Quote for Pest Inspection Services
sections.body: A solid quote clearly breaks down every cost, leaving no room for confusion. Start with the base inspection fee, detailing what type of inspection it is (e.g., visual pest inspection, pre-purchase timber pest inspection). Include any additional services, like thermal imaging for termites or specific pest treatment recommendations, as separate line items. Don't forget travel costs, especially for longer distances. Your time for writing the detailed pest report is also a significant component and should be accounted for in your hourly rate. Always remember to add GST, and make it clear that the total includes it. Using quoting software like QuoteMate helps you quickly generate professional, branded PDF quotes that itemise everything, ensuring transparency. For a standard pre-purchase report, factor in at least 1-2 hours for report generation on top of site time, at your standard hourly rate of $80-$120.

sections.heading: Strategies for Accurate Pricing: How to Quote Pest Inspection Effectively
sections.body: Accurate pricing hinges on knowing your costs and the value of your expertise. Calculate your overheads (insurance, vehicle maintenance, equipment, software, marketing) and add a healthy profit margin. Don't be the cheapest; be the most thorough and transparent. When you learn how to quote pest inspection jobs, consider a tiered pricing structure: basic, standard, and comprehensive. This gives clients options and helps you upsell value. Always confirm the property details before quoting, especially the number of rooms, presence of subfloor access, and roof void accessibility. If you quote blind, you risk losing money on complex jobs. For new clients, offering a clear, detailed quote with a breakdown of a typical termite inspection cost can build immediate trust. A good guideline for profit margin on an inspection service is 20-30% above your operational costs.

sections.heading: Avoiding Cost Traps: Common Mistakes in Pest Inspection Quotes
sections.body: Many tradies lose money by underestimating time or missing key details. A common mistake is not accounting for difficult access points like cramped subfloors or cluttered roof spaces, which significantly extend inspection time. Another trap is failing to specify what is *excluded* from the inspection – for example, areas that are inaccessible without moving heavy furniture or breaking security seals. Clear communication upfront prevents disputes later. Always have a contingency for unexpected findings that might require more detailed analysis or a different report type, but quote for the initial scope. Never assume the property size; verify it. Overlooking the true termite inspection cost or the complexity of a pre-purchase pest inspection can quickly erode your margin. Always confirm the full scope before committing to a price; a verbal estimate can change once you’ve seen the site, but a written quote should be solid for at least 7-14 days.

sections.heading: Delivering Value: Why a Detailed Pest Report Matters for Your Business
sections.body: Your pest report is your key deliverable and a major part of your service's perceived value, justifying the pest report price. A comprehensive report doesn't just list findings; it explains them clearly, provides actionable recommendations, and includes photographic evidence. This level of detail protects both the client and your business. For pre-purchase inspections, adhere strictly to AS 4349.3 requirements, covering timber pests, evidence of previous treatments, and recommendations for further action. A well-written report helps clients understand the property's condition and the implications of any pest activity, often leading to follow-up treatment work for you. For consumer rights and expectations around property reports, check resources like those provided by Fair Trading NSW: https://www.fairtrading.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-property/buying-and-selling-property/property-inspections. Providing a thorough, professional report ensures client satisfaction and generates referrals, making your $450 report worth every cent.

tips: Always specify the property's square metreage on your quote for transparency.
Factor in travel time and fuel costs separately for properties outside your immediate service area.
Use a tiered pricing structure (basic, standard, comprehensive) to suit different client needs.
QuoteMate's line-item suggestions can help ensure you don't miss any critical components of a pest inspection.
For pre-purchase inspections, confirm adherence to AS 4349.3 and clearly state this in your quote.
Include a clause about inaccessible areas and potential extra charges for further investigation.
Regularly review your pricing against your competitors and current operational costs.
Don't just email a quote; follow up with a quick call to answer any questions.

sections.heading: Why Missed Calls Cost Tradies Big Money
sections.body: Every ringing phone that goes unanswered is a potential job walking away. For a tradie, especially a sole operator or small crew, time on the tools means money. But if that means missing calls about new work, you're losing out. Ignoring calls, or simply not being able to answer while you're on a roof or under a house, directly impacts your bottom line. It's not just the lost deposit from one job; it's the ripple effect of not building your client base. Many small business tradies report losing up to $1,000 a week in potential income from unanswered calls. Understanding how to handle missed tradie calls effectively is the first step to turning those missed opportunities into booked jobs. It ensures your business keeps moving forward, even when you're busy with current work.

sections.heading: AI Receptionists: Your New After Hours Tradie Phone Solution
sections.body: An AI receptionist is like having a non-stop, always-on assistant for your phone. These systems answer calls, qualify leads, and even book appointments without you lifting a finger. They're particularly effective for managing the after hours tradie phone, ensuring every enquiry is captured regardless of when it comes in. These VAs work remotely and can answer your phone during set hours, manage your calendar, and even respond to basic customer queries. They offer a personalised touch that AI can't always match, useful for more complex initial client interactions. A virtual assistant can be especially good for tradies who need someone to filter out tyre-kickers from serious leads, or to provide detailed information about your services. You might pay anywhere from $30-$50 an hour for an Australian-based VA, which can be a smart investment if your call volume justifies it and you want a human voice. They help stop tradie missed calls from piling up during your peak hours.

sections.heading: Setting Up Smart Voicemail and SMS Auto-Replies
sections.body: Even without an AI or VA, you can dramatically improve how you manage calls. Combine this with an automated SMS reply for missed calls that includes your website or a link to a simple booking form. This shows professionalism and gives the caller an immediate alternative. This simple setup can significantly reduce small business missed calls and improve customer satisfaction. Look for business phone systems that offer basic auto-reply features, often included for under $50 a month with providers like Telstra or Optus.

sections.heading: Webforms and Social Media for Capturing Leads
sections.body: Not every lead needs a phone call. Set up clear contact forms on your website and use your social media pages to capture enquiries. Many tradies find that a well-designed 'Request a Quote' form on their website, or a direct messaging option on Facebook and Instagram, can catch leads that would otherwise be lost. Make sure these forms are simple to fill out on a mobile phone and ask for all the key information you need to qualify a job. This allows potential clients to reach out when it suits them, even after hours, and provides you with a written record of their needs. This strategy is vital for how to handle missed tradie calls that happen outside of standard working hours, turning passive browsers into active leads.

sections.heading: Tracking Your Calls and Customer Response Times
sections.body: You can't fix what you don't measure. Keep a simple log of missed calls, when they happened, and how long it took you to call back. This helps you spot patterns – maybe you miss most calls during lunch, or between 3-5 PM when you're wrapping up a job. Use a tool like QuoteMate to manage incoming leads from various sources, making sure every inquiry is logged and followed up. Knowing your average response time is key to improving customer service and securing more work. Aim to return calls within a few hours, ideally the same business day. Studies by the Australian Institute of Business indicate that tradies who respond within an hour are significantly more likely to secure the job. You can find more insights on customer response benchmarks at https://www.business.gov.au/marketing/customer-service.

sections.heading: Picking the Best Way to Handle Your Calls
sections.body: The right solution for how to handle missed tradie calls depends on your business size and call volume. For busy sole operators, an AI receptionist or smart voicemail with auto-replies might be enough. For a growing crew, a part-time virtual assistant could be the go. The goal is always the same: ensure no potential customer goes ignored. Start by evaluating how many calls you miss daily and what they're costing you. Test out one solution first, measure its impact, then adjust. Implementing a new system doesn't have to be complicated or expensive, but it needs to be effective. Focus on systems that integrate easily with your existing workflow, so you can keep providing quality service without being tied to your phone. Investing in a robust call management strategy is simply good business sense.

Record a clear, professional voicemail message that guides callers.
Set up an automated SMS reply for any missed calls, including a link to your website.
Use a dedicated business number that can forward calls or go to voicemail.
Train any staff answering calls to qualify leads before passing them to you.
Review your missed call log weekly to identify peak times and adjust strategy.
Consider a CRM like QuoteMate to track all incoming leads from various channels.

sections.heading: Breaking Down After Hours Plumber Call Out Rates
sections.body: When a toilet overflows at 2 AM, clients expect a plumber fast, but they also need a clear quote. Setting your after hours plumber call out rates correctly means breaking down the job into a few key components: a non-negotiable call-out fee, travel time, premium labour costs, and markup on emergency-sourced materials. sections.heading: Setting Your Non-Negotiable After Hours Call Out Fee

This fee covers the overhead of responding to an urgent request outside of normal business hours, including fuel, vehicle wear, and your time getting to the site. A standard after hours call out fee in major Australian cities like Sydney or Melbourne often ranges from $180 to $350, depending on the time of night and your service area. Make sure this fee is clearly itemised on your quote and communicated to the client before you even leave your driveway. It’s essential for compensating you for the disruption to your personal time.

sections.heading: Fair Labour Costs for Emergency Plumber Rates Australia

Typically, this means 1.5x your standard hourly rate for evenings and Saturdays, 2x for Sundays, and 2.5x for public holidays. sections.heading: Quoting Materials for After Hours Plumbing Work

Factor in the time it takes to source these parts – this should be charged at your after-hours labour rate. Never absorb the cost difference yourself; pass it on transparently to the client. Keep a well-stocked van for common emergency items like flexi hoses, tap washers, and standard pipe fittings to minimise extra trips and avoid higher retail prices. For a standard toilet repair, you might spend $20-$150 on parts, which needs to be clearly itemised and marked up.

sections.heading: Dealing with Travel Time and Fuel Costs

guides.title: How Tradies Can Stop Losing Leads and Land More Building Jobs
guides.keyword: how tradies can stop losing leads
guides.description: Australian builders: learn how tradies can stop losing leads through better online presence, smart marketing, and efficient follow-up systems to grow your business.

sections.heading: Act Fast: Why Quick Follow-Up Wins Every Time
sections.body: The quickest way tradies can stop losing leads is to respond immediately. When a potential client calls or messages, they're likely contacting several builders. The first builder to get back to them with a clear, professional response often gets the job. Even if you're on the tools, aim to acknowledge new inquiries within an hour, or at least by the end of your workday. A simple text or email confirming you received their message and will call them back at a specific time is enough. This shows you're organised and keen for their business, setting you apart from slower competition. Losing `tradie phone leads` happens when the client moves on to the next available builder. Getting back to them quickly means you stay in the running for that next extension or reno job. Imagine waiting three days for a quote after asking for one; you'd look elsewhere. Speed matters more than perfect information in that first contact. Your initial response should always be professional, even if it's just to schedule a proper chat. This approach can boost your conversion rate by as much as 30% on initial inquiries.

sections.heading: Build Your Online Presence: Google Business Profile & Website Basics
sections.body: Your online presence acts like your digital workshop, proving you’re a legitimate business. Start with a solid Google Business Profile. It's free and puts you on Google Maps when clients search for builders in your area. Make sure your profile is complete with your services, hours, photos of your work, and current contact details. Keep it updated and encourage clients to leave reviews. Beyond Google, a simple, professional website makes a big difference for `tradie lead generation`. It doesn't need to be complex – a few pages showcasing your best projects, your services, and client testimonials will do. Think of it as a virtual portfolio that potential customers can browse any time. Platforms like Squarespace or Wix offer easy, affordable ways to build one without needing a web developer. Most builders find a basic site costs around $50-$100 per month for hosting and maintenance, a small price for the credibility it provides.

sections.heading: Get Noticed On The Tools: Smart Social Media for Builders
sections.body: Social media isn't just for memes; it's a powerful tool for builders to showcase their craft and attract new clients. Focus on visual platforms like Instagram and Facebook. Post high-quality photos and short videos of your projects from start to finish. Show the before, during, and after. Highlight specific details like joinery, tiling, or custom builds. Use local hashtags (e.g., #SydneyBuilder, #NorthShoreRenovations) to reach people in your service area. Engage with comments and messages promptly. You’re not just posting pictures; you’re building a visual portfolio that speaks to your skill and attention to detail. Sharing progress photos of a kitchen reno or a decking project can keep followers engaged and demonstrate your work ethic. Even a quick 30-second video explaining a design choice can generate significant interest. Aim to post 2-3 times a week for consistent visibility.

sections.heading: Target the Right Clients: Running Profitable Google Ads
sections.body: If you want to speed up `tradie lead generation`, consider running targeted Google Ads. These ads appear at the top of Google search results when someone looks for services like "builder near me" or "home extension Sydney". The key is to be specific with your keywords and target your local area. You control your budget, paying only when someone clicks on your ad. Start with a small daily budget, say $10-$20, and test different ad copy. Focus on what makes your service unique: perhaps you specialise in period home restorations or eco-friendly builds. Track which ads bring in the most qualified inquiries. Google Ads can be a bit of a learning curve, but when set up correctly, they deliver clients who are actively searching for your services right now, leading to immediate job opportunities. Expect a typical cost-per-click for builder-related searches to be around $3-$8, depending on location and competition.

sections.heading: Keep Them Coming Back: Referrals & Reputation Management
sections.body: Repeat business and referrals are the gold standard for any builder, and they’re how tradies can stop losing leads from new sources. Happy clients are your best advertisers. Always aim to exceed expectations, deliver on time and within budget, and maintain clear communication throughout the project. After a job is complete, ask for a review on your Google Business Profile or Facebook page. Positive reviews build trust with potential new clients. Also, politely ask satisfied clients if they know anyone else who might need your services. Offer a small thank-you, like a gift voucher, for successful referrals. Building a strong reputation takes time, but it pays dividends in steady work and less reliance on cold leads. Maintaining a five-star Google rating can boost inbound inquiries by up to 20% compared to a four-star rating.

sections.heading: Automate Your Front Office: Never Miss a Call Again
sections.body: Being on the tools means you can't always answer the phone, which is a common way for tradies to lose leads. Every missed call is a potential job walking away. Many builders rely on voicemail, but callbacks are often delayed, and clients move on. To capture every `builder lead capture` opportunity, consider an AI receptionist. If the phone's ringing while you're on a roof, an AI receptionist like https://callkatie.ai handles the qualifying so you can keep working. These services screen calls, answer common questions, and even book appointments or collect job details, ensuring no lead slips through the cracks, even after hours. This frees you up to focus on the work at hand, knowing your incoming calls are professionally managed.

sections.heading: Quote Right, Win More: Using Your Tools to Lock In Work
sections.body: A professionally prepared quote is often the deciding factor for clients comparing builders. A messy, handwritten quote or a generic spreadsheet won't cut it. Use a dedicated quoting and invoicing app, like QuoteMate, to create clear, branded PDFs. These apps help you itemise materials, labour, and specific tasks accurately, reducing errors that can lead to lost profit or underbidding. They often include features for real-time supplier pricing from places like Bunnings or Reece, ensuring your costs are current. This precision gives the client confidence in your professionalism and helps them understand exactly what they're paying for. A detailed, professional quote can be the difference between winning and losing a job, especially for projects over $10,000. It demonstrates transparency and expertise, making you the preferred choice over competitors who send a quick, vague estimate.

sections.heading: Regular Check-ins: A Monthly Lead Review
sections.body: To truly understand how tradies can stop losing leads, you need to regularly review your lead generation and conversion process. Set aside an hour once a month to look at where your leads are coming from (Google, social, referrals), how quickly you're responding, and how many are converting into paying jobs. Which marketing efforts are working best? Where are you losing potential clients? Maybe your Google Business Profile needs more recent photos, or your follow-up calls are too slow. This consistent review helps you fine-tune your approach, identifying weak points and capitalising on what’s working. Organisations like the Master Builders Association of NSW (https://mbansw.asn.au/) offer resources that can help members refine their business practices, including lead management strategies. Small adjustments based on real data can lead to significant improvements in your bottom line over the year.

tips: Always reply to new inquiries within the hour, even if it's just to acknowledge receipt.
Complete your Google Business Profile with photos, services, and current contact info; encourage reviews.
Post before/during/after project photos on social media platforms like Instagram.
Set a small, targeted budget for Google Ads focusing on local keywords for quick wins.
Ask every satisfied client for a Google review and a referral to friends or family.
Use an AI receptionist to answer calls when you're busy on site; never miss a lead.
Send professional, itemised quotes using an app like QuoteMate to build client trust.
Review your lead sources and conversion rates monthly to spot where jobs are falling through.

guides.title: How Much Should I Charge for Callout Fees? A Tradie's Guide to Fair Pricing
guides.keyword: how much should i charge for callout fees
guides.description: Wondering how much to charge for callout fees as an Aussie tradie? Learn typical rates, influencing factors, and how to set fair, transparent service call charges.

sections.heading: Understanding the Tradie Callout Fee
sections.body: Every tradie knows the phone rings, and often, it's for something small, or a look-see that takes time away from paying work. Figuring out how much should I charge for callout fees is key to not losing money on those quick jobs or initial site visits. A callout fee covers your travel time, fuel, vehicle wear and tear, and the first chunk of your time on site, even if it's just for diagnosis. For builders and other tradies, getting this fee right stops you from driving across town, using your expertise, and walking away with nothing. It’s about valuing your time and making sure every job, big or small, contributes to your bottom line. Underquoting this initial charge is a common mistake that eats into profit quickly.

sections.heading: Typical Callout Fees for Australian Tradies
sections.body: For a standard weekday service call charge during business hours, most Australian tradies charge between $80 to $150. This usually covers the first 30 to 60 minutes on site. Electricians might lean towards the higher end, given licensing and equipment costs, while a general handyman could sit closer to the lower figure. If the job extends beyond that initial time, you then switch to your hourly rate, which typically ranges from $70 to $120 per hour. Always factor in your minimum wage plus overheads when setting these figures. For example, if your travel time averages 20 minutes each way, and your fuel costs are $5 per job, you need to cover that before you even pick up a tool.

sections.heading: Factors Influencing Your Service Call Charge
sections.body: Several things bump your service call charge up or down. Location is a big one; driving 50km out to a rural property usually means a higher callout than a job in the next suburb. Urgency also plays a role. An emergency after-hours call will always cost more than a scheduled repair. Your specialised skills and tools can justify a higher fee too. Think about plumbers needing specific diagnostic equipment for blockages, or electricians needing an expensive thermal camera. If the job requires a specific licence or a second person, that drives up costs. A fair estimate means considering all these moving parts before you set your price.

sections.heading: Emergency and After-Hours Callout Fees
sections.body: When a customer needs you outside standard hours, your callout fee jumps significantly. Expect to charge between $180 and $350 for after-hours work (evenings, weekends), and up to $500 or more for genuine public holiday emergencies. This higher rate compensates for disrupting your personal time, paying penalty rates to any staff you bring, and the immediate response required. It also covers the increased wear and tear on your ute from quick call-outs and potential supply runs when wholesalers are closed. Make sure your clients understand these rates upfront. No one likes a surprise bill when they're already stressed about a burst pipe or no power.

sections.heading: How Callout Fees Integrate with Overall Job Costs
sections.body: Your callout fee should be the base price, not an add-on that confuses the customer. It covers your arrival and initial assessment. After that, you bill for labour and materials. For example, a plumbing callout might be $120. If it takes an extra hour to fix a leaking tap and uses $30 in parts, the total bill is $120 (callout) + $90 (hourly rate) + $30 (materials) = $240. Never double-dip by charging a callout fee and then immediately billing for the first hour of labour if your callout fee already covers that initial time. QuoteMate helps you clearly itemise these costs, so customers see exactly what they're paying for, preventing disputes later on. This transparency builds trust and repeat business.

sections.heading: Setting Your Minimum Job Fee for Tradies
sections.body: Every job needs to be profitable. To figure out your minimum job fee tradies need to calculate their true hourly rate, including all overheads. Don't just pick a number. Add up your weekly costs for insurance, ute payments, fuel, tools, accounting software, and super, then divide by the hours you actually work on the tools. This gives you a baseline hourly rate you must exceed. A minimum job fee might be your callout fee plus your estimated time for a very small task. For instance, an electrician might have a $100 callout, and a minimum job fee of $150 to replace a light switch, covering travel and 30 minutes of work. This ensures you're never running your business at a loss for small tasks. For detailed guidance on consumer rights and fair pricing practices, check resources like the ACCC website: https://www.accc.gov.au.

sections.heading: Communicating Your Callout Fees Clearly
sections.body: Transparency is non-negotiable. Clearly state your callout fee when a customer first enquires. Explain what it includes (e.g., travel, first 30 minutes of work). For urgent or after-hours jobs, confirm the higher rates before heading out. The best practice is to include your callout fee and any minimum job fee tradies use in your written quotes and terms and conditions. Using quoting software like QuoteMate lets you easily generate professional PDFs that detail all charges upfront. This avoids surprises and prevents arguments over the final invoice, making sure your customers feel respected and understand exactly how much should I charge for callout fees and the resulting costs.

tips: Always state your callout fee upfront during the initial call, not just in the quote.
Distinguish between standard, after-hours, and emergency rates clearly.
Factor in your real travel time, fuel, and vehicle costs into your callout fee.
Use a quoting app to itemise your callout fee separately from labour and materials.
Don't discount your callout fee unless it's a strategic decision for a large, ongoing project.
Review your callout fees annually against rising fuel, insurance, and vehicle maintenance costs.
For multi-visit jobs, charge the callout fee once, then bill hourly for subsequent visits.
Keep a record of typical callout fees in your area to stay competitive but profitable.

guides.title: Mastering Bathroom Waterproofing Quotes: How to Quote Bathroom Waterproofing Compliance for Profit
guides.keyword: how to quote bathroom waterproofing compliance
guides.description: Accurate quoting for bathroom waterproofing compliance protects your business and client. Learn the standards, costs, and common pitfalls to quote smarter.

sections.heading: Getting Your Head Around Bathroom Waterproofing Costs
sections.body: When quoting a bathroom reno, the waterproofing isn't just another line item; it's a critical, high-risk component that can sink your margin if you get it wrong. To correctly assess how to quote bathroom waterproofing compliance, you need to factor in membrane materials, labour, and crucial preparation work that often gets overlooked. The average cost for a standard bathroom waterproofing job, including materials and labour, typically sits between $800 and $1,500 for a 5-6 square metre wet area, but this can vary significantly based on the complexity of the layout, the type of membrane chosen, and regional labour rates. For instance, a small powder room might be on the lower end, while a large master ensuite with multiple shower heads and a freestanding bath could easily push past $2,000. Waterproofing failures are not just inconvenient; they're incredibly expensive to rectify, often costing upwards of $10,000 for a major strip-out and re-do. Getting the initial quote right is non-negotiable, safeguarding both your profit and your business reputation. This guide breaks down what to include so your quotes protect you from these common pitfalls.

sections.heading: Australian Standards for Wet Areas: What You Must Know (AS 3740)
sections.body: Compliance with AS 3740 waterproofing is not optional; it's legally required for all wet area construction in Australia. Your quote must reflect the materials and methods that meet this standard, not just the cheapest option available. Specifically, AS 3740 outlines detailed requirements for membrane types, essential substrate preparation, ensuring adequate fall to drains, and precise protection of wall/floor junctions. For example, a waterproof membrane must extend a minimum of 150mm up the wall from the finished floor level in shower areas, and at least 25mm in other wet areas like baths, laundries, or floor waste areas. Showers must have a graded floor with a minimum of 1:100 fall to a waste, and the membrane must terminate directly within the waste opening. Furthermore, specific requirements exist for hobless showers, requiring continuous membrane application. Always check the latest edition of AS 3740, available from https://www.standards.org.au, for detailed specs relevant to your state and project. This ensures your membrane application price covers compliant work that won't fail inspections or lead to callbacks.

sections.heading: Components of a Bulletproof Waterproofing Quote
sections.body: A comprehensive quote for bathroom waterproofing compliance includes several key line items beyond just the membrane itself, ensuring no hidden costs bite you later. Start with thorough substrate preparation, covering cleaning, grinding, patching any holes or cracks, and priming, which can add $80-$250 depending on surface condition and size. Then, specify the waterproof membrane (e.g., a high-quality liquid-applied product like Ardex WPM 001 or Davco K10 Plus, or a sheet membrane), estimating material cost at around $10-$25 per square metre for quality products, factoring in two coats for reliability. Include labour for application, typically 4-8 hours for a standard bathroom, priced at your hourly rate, plus essential curing time between coats and before tiling. Don't forget critical accessories like bond breakers (around $30-$50 per tube for a good polyurethane sealant), corner reinforcements, and puddle flanges (approx. $15-$30 each for stainless steel). Lastly, always account for mandatory inspections; some councils and states require pre-tiling inspections by a building certifier or surveyor, which can cost $200-$400 per visit. Accurately detailing these helps explain your overall wet area waterproofing cost and builds client trust.

sections.heading: Why Compliance Matters and the Risks of Cutting Corners
sections.body: Cutting corners on bathroom waterproofing compliance is a false economy that leads to incredibly costly rectifications and significant legal headaches. Non-compliant work can result in insidious water leaks, extensive structural damage to timber framing or concrete slabs, unsightly mould growth behind walls, and timber rot, all of which are expensive and time-consuming to fix. Repair jobs often involve a complete strip-out and re-do of the bathroom, easily costing upwards of $10,000 to $20,000, not including the disruption to the homeowner. Beyond the substantial financial hit, non-compliance can void your builder's warranty insurance, expose you to legal action under Australian Consumer Law for defects, and severely damage your business reputation, leading to lost future work. As a tradie, you’re legally responsible for ensuring the work meets AS 3740 and the broader National Construction Code (NCC) requirements. An effective way to protect yourself and demonstrate value to your client is to clearly outline how your quote aligns with these stringent standards, ensuring they understand the necessity of a proper membrane application price and the meticulous process involved. This transparency reinforces your professionalism and commitment to quality.

sections.heading: Engaging a Licensed Waterproofer and Inspection Requirements
sections.body: Many Australian states and territories require waterproofing work to be carried out by a licensed waterproofer, and your quote should clearly reflect this professional expertise. For example, in NSW, waterproofing is a specialist licence class, requiring specific qualifications and experience. This licensing ensures the work meets regulatory requirements, provides consumer protection, and typically offers a warranty period for peace of mind. Always include the cost of a licensed professional in your quote; it's a critical component of quality and compliance, not a place to skimp. Furthermore, building permits or local councils often mandate specific inspections before tiling can commence. These inspections verify the correct application of the waterproof membrane and its compliance with AS 3740, the NCC, and local council stipulations. Factor in the certifier's or surveyor's fee, typically $200-$400 per visit, and any potential project delays for inspection scheduling or rectification if initial inspections fail. Clearly explaining these costs and requirements to your client when discussing how to quote bathroom waterproofing compliance is crucial to avoid surprises later and build trust.

sections.heading: Best Practices for Quality & Durability
sections.body: Ensuring quality and long-term durability in bathroom waterproofing goes far beyond just applying a membrane; it starts with meticulous planning, correct material selection, and rigorous execution. Always use high-quality, reputable waterproofing products from trusted suppliers like Bunnings, Reece, or Tradelink, ensuring they are certified and comply with AS 3740. Double-check product data sheets for specific application instructions, optimal temperature ranges, and crucial curing times. Adequate surface preparation, including grinding and thorough cleaning to remove all dust, grease, and contaminants, is paramount for membrane adhesion. Apply bond breakers correctly in all internal corners and around penetrations, as these critical junctions are common failure points. Two coats of membrane are standard best practice, applied at right angles to each other, allowing proper curing between coats as per manufacturer specs. By focusing on these details, your work will stand the test of time, significantly reducing callbacks and safeguarding your professional reputation, making your wet area waterproofing cost a sound, long-term investment for the client. Using a system like QuoteMate helps ensure all these critical line items are included consistently in every quote.

sections.heading: Avoiding Common Waterproofing Quote Mistakes
sections.body: The biggest mistake tradies make when quoting bathroom waterproofing compliance is underestimating the time required for substrate preparation or not accounting for unforeseen substrate issues. Cracks, unstable sub-floors, or residual moisture will compromise any membrane, requiring more labour and materials than initially budgeted. Always allow for adequate drying and curing time for primers and membranes; rushing the job will inevitably lead to failures down the line. Another common error is failing to price in all the ancillary components like puddle flanges for floor wastes, angle fillets, or bond breaker tapes and sealants – these small items collectively add up to significant costs. Forgetting to factor in mandatory inspections or the potential for a re-inspection if the first fails can also quickly eat into your margin. Price for two coats of membrane, even if some products claim single coat performance, as this provides a superior, more durable finish. Always add a 10-15% contingency for unforeseen issues, especially when working on older homes where surprises are common.

tips: Always inspect the substrate thoroughly for moisture or damage before quoting.
Factor in at least two coats of membrane, even if product specs suggest one, for superior durability.
Quote for bond breakers and puddle flanges as standard; they're essential for compliance and longevity.
Specify AS 3740 compliance clearly in every quote to manage client expectations and demonstrate quality.
Allow for mandatory inspection fees (typically $200-$400) and potential re-inspections in your timeline and costs.
Use a quality liquid-applied membrane from reputable suppliers (e.g., Ardex, Davco) and account for curing time.
Add a 10-15% contingency to cover unexpected site conditions or material cost hikes, especially in older builds.

guides.title: How to Quote Epoxy Floor Coating Jobs Right the First Time
guides.keyword: how to quote epoxy floor coating
guides.description: Learn how to accurately quote epoxy floor coating projects in Australia. Cover material costs, prep work, and labour for a profitable job every time.

sections.heading: Getting the Price Right on Epoxy Floor Coating Jobs
sections.body: Many tradies get caught out on epoxy floor coating jobs by underestimating surface prep or material waste. To accurately quote epoxy floor coating, you need to break down every part of the process, from initial assessment to the final topcoat. For sole operators and small crews, missing crucial steps means eating into your margins. This guide walks you through the key cost components, ensuring your quotes are competitive and profitable. Forget just throwing a number out; a proper quote protects your time and reputation. Done right, epoxy floors are a solid earner.

sections.heading: Calculating Floor Area and Your Epoxy Floor Cost Per Square Metre
sections.body: Measure the floor area accurately first. Use a laser measure for precision, then add a 5-10% contingency for waste and unforeseen issues, especially on irregular spaces. Once you have your total square metres, you can estimate your epoxy floor cost per m2 for materials. Most epoxy systems require a primer, a base coat, and one or two topcoats. Check manufacturer specifications for coverage rates per litre; these vary wildly between brands like Sika or Dulux Protective Coatings. Don't forget consumables like rollers, brushes, and mixing paddles. For a typical garage epoxy quote, expect material costs to be a significant portion, so getting this calculation spot-on is critical. Always pull current pricing from suppliers like Bunnings or specific industrial coating distributors.

sections.heading: Selecting Epoxy Types and Their Impact on Your Quote
sections.body: The type of epoxy system drastically affects your material costs and application complexity. Standard two-part epoxy is a common choice, but options like polyaspartic flooring price higher due to faster cure times and superior UV resistance, making them ideal for outdoor areas or quick turnarounds. Urethane cement systems offer even greater chemical and thermal shock resistance, often specified for commercial kitchens. Hybrid systems might combine different properties. Always confirm the client's needs and the floor's intended use before spec'ing materials. Higher-end systems from suppliers like Hychem or Parchem will have different pricing tiers compared to general-purpose options. Make sure your quote clearly specifies the exact product series you're using.

sections.heading: Pricing Essential Surface Preparation for Longevity
sections.body: Surface preparation is the foundation of any good epoxy job; skimping here guarantees callbacks. Your quote must include mechanical grinding or shot blasting to achieve the required Concrete Surface Profile (CSP) – usually CSP 2-3 for most applications. Factor in the hire cost for equipment like floor grinders from Kennards Hire, along with diamond tooling. Repairing cracks, divots, and spalling with epoxy patch compounds is also a must. Moisture testing using a calcium chloride test kit (ASTM F1869) or a moisture metre should be part of your initial assessment, as high moisture content requires vapour barrier primers, adding to material and labour costs. See guidance on concrete surface preparation at https://www.concrete.org.au/.

sections.heading: Estimating Labour Hours and Crew Needs
sections.body: Labour is often the largest component of an epoxy floor coating quote. Break it down into discrete tasks: initial cleaning, grinding, crack repairs, vacuuming, priming, base coat application, and topcoat application. Each coat typically requires a separate visit due to cure times, adding to travel and setup. A standard garage (around 36m2) might take one tradie a full day for prep and primer, then two half-days for subsequent coats, factoring in drying. Larger or more complex sites with multiple colours or flake systems will require more crew and longer on-site times. Don't forget to factor in your hourly rate for travel to and from the site, and allow extra time for unforeseen site conditions or access issues.

sections.heading: Including Overheads, Contingencies, and Final Touches
sections.body: A comprehensive quote covers more than just materials and direct labour. Account for your business overheads like insurance, vehicle running costs, and administrative time. Always include a contingency of 10-15% for unexpected issues such as excessive concrete repairs, tricky access, or weather delays. Disposal of old flooring materials or empty product drums also needs pricing in. If the client wants intricate designs, line marking, or a specific anti-slip aggregate, these are additional line items. Remember to clearly separate the GST on your quote. Software like QuoteMate helps you manage line items, apply GST, and produce professional PDF quotes and invoices for your clients, making sure nothing is missed.

sections.heading: Avoiding Common Costly Mistakes When Quoting Epoxy
sections.body: The biggest trap when you quote epoxy floor coating is underestimating the prep. A rough concrete slab will always take longer and use more material than a smooth one. Don't assume the client has cleared the area; specify what needs to be moved and who is responsible. Another common mistake is failing to account for accessibility. Is it a tight stairwell, a busy loading dock, or an empty warehouse? Harder access means more labour. Always visit the site. Relying on photos or client descriptions alone will lead to missed details and eaten profit. Always check the current supplier prices for all your materials, as these can fluctuate without warning.

tips: Always do a site visit; never quote epoxy sight unseen.
Factor in a 5-10% material waste contingency for every job.
Specify the exact epoxy system and brand in your quote to avoid confusion.
Charge extra for crack repairs or any surface defects found during prep.
Allow for multi-day cure times in your labour estimates and scheduling.
Include equipment hire costs (grinders, vacuums) as a separate line item.
Ensure your quote clearly states what is and isn't included, like furniture moving.
Use current pricing from major suppliers like Bunnings or industrial coating distributors.

guides.title: Mastering Pool Fencing: How to Quote Pool Fencing Installation Accurately
guides.keyword: how to quote pool fencing installation
guides.description: Accurate pool fence quotes prevent costly errors. Learn to price materials, labour, and compliance for any pool fencing installation job in Australia.

sections.heading: Understanding the True Pool Fencing Costs in Australia
sections.body: Quoting pool fencing installation isn't just about slapping a price on glass panels; it's about accounting for every variable that impacts the final pool fence cost Australia wide. The biggest blowouts happen from overlooked site specifics and non-compliant installations. Get these right, and your quote holds up. When you're putting together a quote, consider the site's slope, soil type, and access. A simple flat-ground install with clear access is a world away from a job on a sloping backyard with tight entry for materials. For an average residential job, expect material costs to be between $150-$450 per lineal metre, before labour. Overlooking these early details means you'll eat into your margin later on, especially if you have to bring in extra gear or labour. Always start with a detailed site visit.

sections.heading: Material Choices: Aluminium, Glass, and Timber Pricing
sections.body: The choice of material significantly dictates the final cost and installation method. Aluminium panel fencing is a popular choice for its durability and lower cost. Expect to quote between $80-$150 per lineal metre for basic aluminium panels from suppliers like Bunnings or Stratco, not including posts or gates. For a sleek glass pool fence quote, fully framed options start around $180-$350 per lineal metre, while frameless glass, which requires heavy-duty spigots, can push costs to $350-$600 per lineal metre, or even higher for custom sizes. Timber fences, while less common for pool surrounds due to maintenance, might be around $70-$120 per lineal metre for treated pine. Always check your current supplier prices from places like Reece or Tradelink for fittings and spigots, as these can fluctuate often. Using accurate, real-time pricing ensures your margins are locked in from the start.

sections.heading: Site Assessment and Precise Measurements for Your Quote
sections.body: Accurate measurements are the bedrock of any solid pool fencing quote. Missing a corner or miscalculating a gate opening means reordering panels or cutting expensive glass on-site, which costs time and money. Always measure twice, using a laser measurer for precision, especially on uneven ground. Document the entire perimeter, noting any existing structures, retaining walls, or garden beds that will impact post placement. Identify potential issues like buried services or rock formations that might require specialised digging equipment. For example, installing 12mm frameless glass panels (typically 1200mm high) on a hard-rock site will add $30-$50 per post hole for rock drilling, compared to standard soil. Factor in extra time and materials for any non-standard angles or custom panel requirements. A detailed site sketch with dimensions and notes on ground conditions helps avoid disputes later.

sections.heading: Labour & Installation: Pricing Your Time and Skill
sections.body: Your labour is a significant part of the pool fencing cost Australia clients pay. Don't underprice your expertise. Calculate your crew's hourly rate, including on-costs like superannuation, insurance, and vehicle expenses. A two-person crew for a straightforward 20-metre aluminium fence might take 1-2 days, while a complex frameless glass installation over a similar distance could easily take 3-4 days, especially with custom cutting or difficult access. Set your hourly rate for skilled labour at a minimum of $80-$120 per person, per hour, for standard installs. Remember to factor in travel time to and from the site, as well as time spent picking up materials. For heavy-duty lifting, like with large glass panels, you might need specialised suction lifters, which can cost $50-$100 per day to hire. Clearly itemise labour hours in your quote so the client understands the value of your work.

sections.heading: Navigating Regulations and Ensuring Pool Fence Compliance
sections.body: Pool fence compliance is non-negotiable and varies slightly by state, but all Australian pool fences must meet AS 1926.1-2012. This standard dictates minimum fence heights (1200mm), gate self-closing and self-latching mechanisms, and non-climbable zones. Failure to comply can lead to hefty fines for homeowners and rework for you. Always factor in time for understanding local council requirements and potential inspection costs. Some councils charge $150-$300 for a final inspection certificate. Specify that your quote includes materials and installation to meet AS 1926.1-2012, and advise the client on their responsibility for ongoing certification. For detailed compliance info, refer to your state's building regulator or https://www.standards.org.au for access to the Australian Standards.

sections.heading: Gates, Latches, and Additional Features for an Accurate Quote
sections.body: Gates and their hardware are critical for both safety and functionality, and they’re often where extra costs sneak into a pool fencing job. Self-closing and self-latching gates are a mandatory part of pool fence compliance. Standard spring-loaded hinges and magnetic latches cost between $80-$200 per gate set, but upgrade options like hydraulic soft-closing hinges or key-lockable latches can cost upwards of $300-$500 per gate. Also consider additional features such as custom panel shapes for unique landscaping, extra gate widths for accessibility, or the integration of a child-safety pool alarm. Each custom element adds to material and labour time. Clearly list these as separate line items in your QuoteMate proposal. For instance, a custom raked glass panel for a sloping section might add 30-50% to the cost of a standard panel, plus additional design and cutting time.

sections.heading: Final Quote Review and Contingency Planning
sections.body: Before sending off any pool fencing quote, give it a thorough once-over. Ensure all measurements are double-checked, material costs are current, and labour estimates are realistic. It’s smart to build a small contingency — around 5-10% — into your quote for unforeseen issues, especially on older properties or sites with tricky access. This isn't padding; it's smart business for potential ground surprises or slight material price bumps. Don’t forget to include GST in your final figure. Present your quote clearly, perhaps with different options for materials, so the client can choose what suits their budget. An organised quote built with an app like QuoteMate makes it easy to add detailed line items and present a professional estimate.

Factor in extra labour time for rock drilling or difficult site access.

Measure the pool fence perimeter precisely; a laser measurer is your best mate.

spokes.title: How to Chase Unpaid Invoices in Australia

spokes.metaDescription: What to do when a client doesn't pay. The exact escalation path Australian tradies should follow at 7, 14, 30 and 60 days overdue, plus the legal options most don't know.
spokes.intro: An unpaid invoice is one of the most expensive problems in trade. Time spent chasing is time not earning, and the longer an invoice sits past due, the lower the chance you'll ever collect it. The good news is there's a clear escalation path that resolves most cases inside 30 days without lawyers and without burning the relationship.

sections.heading: Day 1–7: Friendly reminder
sections.body: Most overdue invoices aren't deliberate — clients forget, lose the email, or are waiting on their own customer to pay. A polite SMS or email on day 1 past due, then a follow-up at day 7, resolves the majority of cases. Keep the tone neutral and assume good faith. QuoteMate sends these automatically with templates that mention the invoice number, amount, due date, and a one-click payment link, so the client can pay without digging up the original invoice.

sections.heading: Day 14–30: Formal demand
sections.body: If two reminders haven't worked, escalate to a formal letter of demand. State the original invoice details, total amount owing, any late-payment interest if specified in your terms, and a final pay-by date (usually 7 days). Reference your right to apply interest under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts standard (typically 8%–10% p.a. for B2B work) if you included it in your original quote. Most disputes get resolved at this stage because the client now sees you're documenting the trail.

sections.heading: Day 30+: Tribunals and debt collection
sections.body: For amounts under $25,000 (NSW NCAT, VIC VCAT) or $20,000 (QLD QCAT), small claims tribunals are cheap, fast, and don't require a lawyer. Filing fees are around $50–$200 and you can usually get a hearing inside 8 weeks. For larger debts or commercial work, a debt collection agency (typically 10%–25% commission) is faster than court. The key is to have your trail documented: original quote, signed acceptance, invoice, reminders, demand letter. QuoteMate keeps all of this in one place per client.

faqs.question: Can I charge interest on overdue invoices in Australia?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it was specified in your original quote or contract terms. Standard rates are 8%–10% per annum for B2B debts. For consumer (residential) work, you'll need this clearly stated upfront.

faqs.question: What's the cheapest way to recover an unpaid invoice?
faqs.answer: Send a formal letter of demand first. If that doesn't work, your state's small claims tribunal (NCAT, VCAT, QCAT, etc.) is cheaper and faster than court for amounts under $20,000–$25,000.

faqs.question: Should I use a debt collector?
faqs.answer: For larger debts ($5,000+) or commercial clients, yes — debt collectors usually charge 10%–25% commission but are faster than court. For smaller residential debts, a tribunal is usually better value.

spokes.title: Taking Deposits Legally in Australia
spokes.summary: Maximum deposit amounts are capped by law in most Australian states. The actual numbers, by state, plus how to take a deposit without getting sideways with consumer protection.
spokes.metaTitle: Taking Deposits Legally for Tradies (Australia 2026) | QuoteMate
spokes.metaDescription: How much deposit can you legally ask for as an Australian tradie? The exact caps in NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, ACT and Tasmania, plus the safest way to take a deposit.
spokes.intro: Asking for a deposit before starting a job is completely legal in Australia — but the maximum amount is capped by state-based home building laws. Get this wrong and you can be hit with fines, forced refunds, or have your contractor licence reviewed. The good news: the rules are simple once you know them.

sections.heading: Maximum deposits by state
sections.body: For domestic building work, the typical legal maximums are: NSW (Home Building Act) — 10% for jobs over $20,000, no cap for smaller jobs but reasonableness applies; VIC (Domestic Building Contracts Act) — 10% for contracts under $20,000, 5% for contracts $20,000+; QLD (QBCC) — 10% for jobs over $3,300, 20% for off-site (prefab) components; SA (Building Work Contractors Act) — generally 10%; WA (Home Building Contracts Act) — 6.5% for contracts $7,500+; ACT — 10% for residential building work over $12,000; TAS — no statutory cap but consumer law fairness rules apply. Always check your state regulator's current rules before the contract is signed.

sections.heading: Deposits vs. progress payments
sections.body: A deposit is the up-front payment that secures the job, locks in your schedule, and covers initial material orders. Progress payments are the staged payments you receive as the job hits milestones (e.g., demo complete, frame up, lock-up, completion). For trade work over $20,000, structuring progress payments correctly is more important than the deposit size — it's how you stay cash-flow-positive on long jobs without being out-of-pocket on materials.

sections.heading: How to take a deposit safely
sections.body: Three rules. First, never take a deposit before the customer has accepted the quote in writing — a signed quote, an emailed acceptance, or a digital signature inside an app like QuoteMate is fine. Second, issue a deposit invoice that itemises what the deposit covers (materials, scheduling, etc.) and clearly references the parent quote. Third, pay the deposit straight into your business account, not personal. QuoteMate handles all three automatically: when a customer accepts a quote, it generates the deposit invoice and takes the payment via Square — Tap to Pay on the spot, or a hosted online link the customer pays from their phone — and logs everything against the job. If you'd rather not absorb the card fee, the optional 2.9% surcharge passthrough adds it to the customer's total.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a 50% deposit?
faqs.answer: Generally no, not for domestic building work. Most Australian states cap deposits at 5%–10% of the contract value. Always check your state's current home building regulator (NSW Fair Trading, VBA in Victoria, QBCC in Queensland, etc.).

faqs.question: What if the deposit cap is too low to cover materials?
faqs.answer: Use progress payments. For a $30,000 job, take a 5%–10% deposit on signing, then schedule progress payments at milestones (e.g., materials delivered, work commenced, halfway, completion). This keeps you cash-flow-positive without breaking deposit law.

faqs.question: Do deposit caps apply to commercial work?
faqs.answer: Most state laws apply specifically to 'domestic building work' for residential customers. Commercial contracts have more flexibility but should still be governed by clear written terms.

The deposit invoice is auto-generated and the payment is logged automatically. If you'd rather not absorb the card fee, the optional 2.9% surcharge passthrough adds it to the customer's total.

The combination roughly doubles the chance of getting paid on the first reminder. The catch is that SMS costs money to send (typically a few cents per message) and you should never send more than 2–3 SMS per overdue invoice — anything more crosses the line into nuisance and can damage the relationship. sections.heading: Templates that actually get a response
sections.body: Three things make a reminder convert: a clear subject line that mentions the invoice number, a polite but specific tone (no passive-aggression, but no vague 'just checking in' either), and a payment link that takes the customer one tap away from settling. Avoid attaching a PDF of the invoice — most people don't open them on phones. Instead, summarise in plain text: 'Hi {first name}, this is a reminder that invoice #{number} for ${amount} was due {date}. You can pay here: {link}.' faqs.answer: A 4-touch cadence works for most jobs: 1 day before due, 1 day after due, 7 days after due, 14 days after due. After that, escalate to a formal letter of demand.

faqs.question: Will automated reminders annoy my customers?

Some tradies post them publicly (with the customer's consent) on a portfolio gallery — QuoteMate can export photo bundles per job for that purpose. faqs.question: Where are photos stored?

faqs.question: Can I annotate after taking the photo?

faqs.question: Do photos sync across my devices?

faqs.question: Can I attach photos to a quote PDF?

sections.heading: Why the quote's materials list isn't enough

A bathroom reno quote might say 'tile floor and walls, install vanity'. The checklist for the day says: 'pick up extra bag of grout in case, drop sheets, take the multi-tool not the recip saw, ring Reece by 7am to confirm vanity is at the branch'. sections.heading: How the checklist works in QuoteMate

The checklist lives with the job, so the items you wrote when quoting are still there on the day you do the work, three weeks later. When the job's complete, the checklist stays attached to the record, so the next similar job you can copy the checklist forward and start with the same list, ticked clean.

sections.heading: Reusing checklists across similar jobs

faqs.question: Is the checklist the same as the materials list?

faqs.question: Can I tick items off offline?

faqs.question: Can I copy a checklist from a previous job?

faqs.question: Does the checklist appear on the customer's quote?

faqs.question: How many items can I add?

spokes.title: Automated Quote Follow-Ups for Tradies

spokes.intro: The single biggest reason tradies lose work isn't price — it's silence. sections.heading: Why most quotes that lose actually just go cold

The tradie who sends one well-timed reminder converts a chunk of those quotes that would otherwise stay 'pending' forever. faqs.question: Will customers be annoyed by the follow-ups?
faqs.answer: Not at the default cadence (day 3, 7, 14). The templates are written in plain tradie English with the actual price and a payment link — most customers find them helpful because they'd forgotten. If a customer replies, the sequence stops automatically.

faqs.question: Can I customise the follow-up templates?

faqs.question: Does QuoteMate send follow-ups by SMS?
faqs.answer: On the Pro plan, yes. SMS follow-ups send from your business name and have a much higher open rate than email — most tradies use email for the day-3 nudge and switch to SMS at day 7.

faqs.question: What if I want to stop follow-ups on a specific quote?
faqs.answer: Open the quote, tap the actions sheet, and toggle follow-ups off. You can also push the first follow-up date out to a custom date if the customer asked for time.

faqs.question: Do follow-ups affect quoted-to-accepted conversion?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tradies using the default cadence typically see meaningful uplift in quote conversion rate, especially on residential work — the same quotes still convert, they just convert sooner and more of them stop sitting in 'pending' forever.
